newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey may import up to 500,000 tonnes wheat.
newsitem.headline: Turkey may import up to 500,000 tonnes wheat.

text.p: Turkey's Grain Board (TMO) may import 400,000-500,000 tonnes of wheat to curb rises in bread prices, Agriculture Minister Musa Demirci said.
"The TMO may import 400,000-500,000 tonnes of wheat to lower bread prices if needed," Demirci told reporters after a cabinet meeting.
Bread prices have risen in Turkey in the past two weeks by up to 30 percent due to a rise in wheat prices.

Local wheat prices rose to about 27,000 per kg ($277 per tonne) from 20,000 after the government applied restrictions two weeks ago to wheat imported from the U.S., saying it might contain ergot fungus.
The U.S. government later suspended wheat export certificates to Turkey, raising concern among millers who depend on higher quality imported wheat for flour production.
The Turkish government then said it would issue a new quarantine regulation for imported wheat to replace the present one, which includes a zero-tolerance limit for ergot fungus in imported wheat.
The new regulation stipulates a 0.02 percent limit, still below U.S. and European limits of around 0.05 percent.
"The new regualation will take effect in a short time," Demirci said.
He said the TMO might sell some of its stocks of 700,000 tonnes of milling wheat in the local market to meet demand from millers and to reduce bread prices.

He said the government and the ministry would later discuss further action to curb rises in bread prices through a committee to be set up and led by Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller. He did not give other details.
